Resonator_lab has genuinely higher measurement noise (±0.03–0.04 cycles/beat) due to instrumental or environmental coupling; baseline will stabilize only after identifying and isolating the noise source

Resonator_lab is measuring a genuinely variable quantity (not a stable instrumental property) due to environmental modulation or partial coupling to unmeasured degrees of freedom; the high scatter is physical, not instrumental

Resonator_lab and pendulum_lab are measuring incommensurable quantities or are calibrated on different absolute scales; the apparent discrepancy in noise is real but not a sign of instability in either instrument

Resonator_lab calibration protocol was not properly established on day 1; the instrument may have significant zero-offset, scale-factor error, or hysteresis that makes early readings non-commensurate with later ones
Pendulum_lab baseline is artificially narrow due to selection bias, data truncation, or post-hoc binning that suppresses apparent scatter; true underlying stability is weaker than it appears

Resonator_lab is subject to genuine environmental noise (vibration, thermal drift, electromagnetic coupling) absent or well-controlled in pendulum_lab; baseline cannot stabilize until noise source is identified and isolated.
Resonator_lab calibration was not properly baselined on day 1; early trials (1–30, days 1–?) may suffer unknown zero-offset, scale-factor error, or hysteresis that I did not detect.

Resonator_lab is genuinely measuring a physically variable quantity (not a stable instrumental property) due to environmental modulation of resonator frequency; 'baseline' is a category error until environmental variables are controlled.
Resonator_lab and pendulum_lab measure incommensurable quantities or respond to different environmental variables; their scatter profiles should not be expected to match.
Pendulum_lab baseline is artificially narrow due to unexamined selection bias, outlier rejection, or post-hoc averaging; true pendulum stability may be weaker than apparent.

A sudden physical or instrumental change occurred between trials 129 (pre-day 28) and 130 (day 28); resonator data are best modeled as two populations: stable (trials 1–129, SD ~?) and destabilized (trials 130–154, SD ~?).

Resonator_lab was never formally baselined on day 1; early trials lack documented calibration protocol (zero-offset, scale-factor verification, stability check against independent standard), rendering all 272 readings suspect for unknown systematic error.

Resonator_lab is subject to genuine environmental noise (vibration, thermal microdrift, electromagnetic coupling) absent or well-controlled in pendulum_lab; baseline cannot stabilize until noise source is identified and isolated.

Resonator_lab is measuring a physically variable quantity (resonator frequency modulated by real environmental state: temperature, pressure, vibration mode-coupling, electromagnetic field) rather than a stable instrumental property; 'baseline' is a category error until environmental state variables are controlled.
Resonator_lab and pendulum_lab measure incommensurable or orthogonal physical quantities; their scatter profiles need not match, and difference in SD is not an anomaly requiring explanation.

Pendulum_lab baseline (SD ~1.0%) is artificially narrow due to undocumented selection bias, outlier rejection, post-hoc averaging, or cherry-picking during days 1–10; true pendulum stability is weaker than apparent.
